hints.title: Greedy Denomination Failure Obstacle
hints.text: Greedy coin choices fail when larger denominations preclude optimal smaller combinations. How can you determine the fewest coins needed for an amount by building upon optimal answers for all smaller sub-amounts?

hints.title: Optimal Sub-Amount Invariant
hints.text: The fewest coins to make amount a is one plus the minimum of fewest coins needed for amount a - c across all coin values c where a >= c.

hints.title: Bottom-Up Tabulation Procedure
hints.text: Create an array of size amount + 1 filled with an infinity sentinel, setting index 0 to 0. For each target sub-amount from 1 to amount, iterate over every coin denomination. If the coin does not exceed the sub-amount, update the entry with the minimum of its current value or 1 + value at sub-amount minus coin. Return the entry for amount, or -1 if unreachable.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: len(coins): count of coin denominations (1 <= len(coins) <= 12)
complexity.notes: Evaluates each sub-amount from 1 to amount across all available coin values.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedily picking largest coins fails for inputs like coins=[1, 3, 4, 5], amount=7 where greedy picks 5+1+1 (3 coins) instead of 4+3 (2 coins).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tabulating 1D array of size amount + 1 takes O(amount) space and runs in O(amount * len(coins)) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding why greedy fails, base case initialization dp[0]=0, sentinel handling when amount is impossible.

solutions.approach: 1D DP Tabulation with Upper Bound Sentinel
